finding: The old 2.65x mean TTFT difference is not reproduced under the same controlled arrival pattern. Closed-loop arrival feedback and server queueing are supported as important contributors; no intrinsic 2.65x first-token compute penalty is established.
production_patch_reason: No confirmed framework timing defect or isolated optimization target; controlled diagnostic observation was implemented instead.
known_limits: Diagnostic timing and metrics enabled for every configuration; these are not uninstrumented benchmark throughput measurements.
Each configuration was run as a group; three rounds and few solo samples are descriptive controls, not production tail-latency guarantees.
Fixed-arrival paced load has a lower offered load than saturated closed-loop concurrency32; report it as a separate load regime.
The framework forward-to-prefill-finished interval is wall time, not isolated GPU execution time.
No original-run server queue_time exists; this diagnostic cannot retroactively fill it.
Exact GPU critical-path costs and why fixed3 completion times dephase were not independently isolated.
The independent SSE client shares the first-nonempty-text definition, but differs from the native benchmark implementation; absolute cross-client differences are not optimization gains.
